messages:
olga: Quick note — onboarding sampleapp failed yesterday during smoke tests. REST health endpoint (/v1/health) returns 200 but SDK call throws 401 and stops. Guessing parity gap.
ryan: hmm. SDK v2 only wrapped /v1/status and model endpoints, we never added a dedicated health wrapper. It does have generic request() though.
jess: ah that explains it. sampleapp calls sdk.health() expecting same semantics as curl -> restful response. SDK currently treats 401 as permanent auth failure (no refresh) and surfaces error to app.
olga: sampleapp uses ephemeral keys + server-side refresh flow. REST client was refreshing token automatically via existing middleware so tests passed. SDK not doing that caused weird onboarding friction.
ryan: right — SDK doesn't auto-refresh; designed that way to avoid implicit network calls during simple clients. But we should document it, or add an opt-in autoRefresh flag.
jess: tiny repro I used:
```
# REST
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $EPHEMERAL" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/health
# SDK (node)
await client.health()
```
REST -> 200, SDK -> throws AuthenticationError: 401

olga: Noticed user confusion in onboarding logs: "health check failed" then they open support ticket. Friction > churn.
ryan: proposal: 1) add README note under SDK auth that SDK will not auto-refresh tokens; 2) add convenience helper `client.withAutoRefresh(refreshFn)` or `client.config.autoRefresh=true` for apps using ephemeral keys; 3) add health wrapper that mirrors REST semantics.
jess: I can PR docs for point 1 today. Will add code snippet showing how to wrap health using generic request as interim:
```
const res = await client.request({ method: 'GET', path: '/v1/health' })
if (res.status !== 200) throw new Error('unhealthy')
```
olga: Can someone take item 2? This would reduce support load. If it's small, we could ship in patch release.
ryan: I can prototype autoRefresh helper. Will check security review first (we don't want auto-refresh to leak refresh tokens). ETA EOD tomorrow for a design doc.
jess: noted — I'll link the onboarding ticket and add a snippet to the quickstart troubleshooting section: https://redwood.dev/docs/sdk/auth#ephemeral-keys
deploy-bot: Deployed branch docs/quickstart-fix to staging (build 2026-03-22_21:03)
olga: awesome — thanks. Let's also add a short note in the sampleapp README so customers using ephemeral flows don't hit this silent failure.
ryan: filing GH issue now -> https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/issues/412
jess: assigning myself to docs PR. thanks! :thumbsup:
